name: Mediabunny server extension
role: Adds FFmpeg-backed codecs and hardware acceleration to Mediabunny in Node, Bun, Deno
summary: @mediabunny/server registers a NodeAV backend (bindings to FFmpeg's C API) so Mediabunny can encode and decode AVC, HEVC, VP8, VP9, AV1 and ProRes, plus AAC, MP3, Opus, FLAC, AC-3 and others, outside the browser. Adds resize, rotate, flip and crop transforms and hardware acceleration on macOS, Linux and Windows. Same Mediabunny API server-side as in the browser.
use_when: Same Mediabunny TypeScript code must run in Node with codecs WebCodecs lacks
Server-side TS pipeline wanting FFmpeg codecs without shelling out to a CLI
avoid_when: Filtergraphs, overlays or muxing control: ffmpeg-ffprobe directly
Simple delivery encodes in scripts: the ffmpeg CLI has fewer moving parts
Browser use: base mediabunny plus WebCodecs
license: MPL-2.0 per npm; confirm in the package LICENSE, and the bundled FFmpeg build's own licence terms
notes: Separate package from mediabunny; evaluate independently.

2026-10-26: npm lists MPL-2.0 for @mediabunny/server; the docs page does not state a licence, so the earlier 'may be commercial' caution is unconfirmed. Whether NodeAV's bundled FFmpeg is LGPL or GPL was not checked.
2026-10-26: published in lockstep with mediabunny (1.62.1); maturity not labelled in the docs.

assessment.rationale: Published 2026-10-22 in lockstep with mediabunny; npm licence MPL-2.0. Adds FFmpeg-grade codecs to Node via NodeAV. Narrow value over the FFmpeg CLI; keep as catalogued for TypeScript-only pipelines.
